method.offline_note: resolution goes to the configured index (PyPI) unless artifacts are in pip's cache; build isolation installs setuptools/wheel from the index. --ignore-installed makes the resolved set independent of the measuring venv. Set PIP_NO_INDEX=1 only if a pre-populated cache is acceptable for a re-run.
method.wheel_note: pip performs a real PEP 517 metadata build in an isolated env to obtain the wheel METADATA; --dry-run means the wheel is discarded, not installed. No wheel is retained; build isolation was observed per case.
method.report_capture: written to a file (not '-'): on pip 26.2.1 stdout also carries progress lines, so --report - would not be parseable as pure JSON
method.isolation_of_subject_source: each subject is copied to lanes/B/staging/<id>/ before measuring; a PEP 517 build writes *.egg-info into the source dir, so measuring in place would mutate the repo

network_measured.interpretation: counts of 'Downloading ' and 'Using cached' lines over all cases; 0 downloads means every artifact came from pip's local HTTP cache, so this particular run needed no live index access -- a cold cache would (offline is false, not verified offline).

method.repeatability: sorted set comparison; identical inputs give identical resolved sets

proves: exactly which keys [project.optional-dependencies] declares in the three measured pyproject.toml artifacts (and that all three declare none)
pip 26.x on CPython 3.12/Windows returns exit 0 and prints 'does not provide the extra' for a nonexistent extra, with a resolved set identical to the no-extra baseline
a declared extra (fixture: yaml=[PyYAML>=6]) resolves an additional distribution, so the measurement can distinguish 'provided' from 'absent'
the same silent-equality behaviour for a near-miss typo (yaml vs yamlx) on the fixture
does_not_prove: that any code path in hg-kseos actually needs these extras, or that the app works with them installed (no import, no runtime check was performed)
anything about wheels built by uv/CI rather than by pip's PEP 517 isolated build
behaviour on other pip versions, other Python versions, or offline resolution
that a downstream checker actually reads these fields -- the contract is a proposal
that 'INSTALL_OK: exit 0' style gates elsewhere in the pipeline were fixed
claim_ceiling.evidence_class: measurement of pip CLI semantics + static parse of pyproject.toml artifacts
claim_ceiling.not_a_substitute_for: an integration test that imports the extras-gated module

previous_round_recheck.claim_under_test: pip install .[yaml] exited 0 on all three trees and therefore 'extra install' had been treated as a qualification step
previous_round_recheck.instrument: same pip, but resolved sets are diffed instead of reading exit code

contract.purpose: Decide whether an extra is REALLY provided, using only fields that differ between an existing and a non-existing extra. Exit code does NOT: an absent extra exits 0.

extras_declared.source: tomllib: [project.optional-dependencies] keys of the subject pyproject.toml
extras_declared.accept: [] when the table is absent; otherwise the exact declared key set
extras_declared.why: static ground truth; an extra that is not here cannot be provided

extras_metadata_provided.source: pip --report install[].metadata.provides_extra of the local project entry
extras_metadata_provided.accept: subset of extras_declared (normalized); disagreement => builder drops extras
extras_metadata_provided.why: proves the extra survived into the built wheel METADATA, not just the toml

extras_installable.source: computed: extras whose dry-run resolved >=1 distribution absent from baseline
extras_installable.accept: must equal the required extras exactly; [] means no extra installs anything
extras_installable.why: the only behavioural proof that the extra pulls dependencies

extras_noop_attempted.source: computed: extra declared in metadata but resolved delta == baseline
extras_noop_attempted.accept: [] (a declared-but-empty extra is a defect, not a pass)
extras_noop_attempted.why: catches EXTRA_NOOP: 'successful' install that installs nothing extra

extras_absent_rejected.source: computed: extra names requested in the probe that are not declared
extras_absent_rejected.accept: non-empty only for deliberately nonexistent names (probe proof)
extras_absent_rejected.why: proves the probe itself would notice a typo; must never contain a required extra

exit_code.accept: 0 -- recorded for the record, but NEVER used as the pass condition
exit_code.why: absent extra returns 0; using exit code as the gate is the original false green

stderr_has_extra_warning.accept: true iff stderr contains 'does not provide the extra'; advisory only
stderr_has_extra_warning.why: a warning alone is not a failure signal in pip; and pip prints it on stderr, which CI frequently discards

resolved_distributions.accept: 'name==version' strings, sorted; compared as a set per subject
resolved_distributions.why: the raw material for the delta; the pip report does not record which extras were requested, so the diff is the only place extras become visible

verdict_code.why: single machine-readable decision derived from the fields above

verdict_rules.EXTRA_PROVIDED: extra in provides_extra AND resolved delta has >=1 addition
verdict_rules.EXTRA_NOOP: extra in provides_extra AND resolved delta == baseline
verdict_rules.EXTRA_ABSENT: extra not in provides_extra (pip warns, exit stays 0, delta == baseline)
verdict_rules.BASELINE: no extra requested; the diff reference point

contract.pass_rule: PASS iff exit_code == 0 for every case AND required_extras ⊆ extras_declared AND required_extras == extras_installable AND extras_noop_attempted == [] AND extras_absent_rejected ∩ required_extras == {}

fail_codes.EXTRA_ABSENT: requested extra is not declared -> the install silently equals the default
fail_codes.EXTRA_NOOP: extra is declared but resolves nothing -> same silent equality
fail_codes.EXTRA_METADATA_DRIFT: declared in toml but absent from wheel Provides-Extra

computation_notes: extras_installable and extras_noop_attempted are empty for a subject with no declared extras -- 'no extras' is not the same claim as 'extras work'.
Extra names are PEP 685 normalized (lowercase, [-_.]+ -> '-') before comparison.
Compare resolved sets, not counts: a version bump inside the default set would change counts without any extra being involved.
Use --ignore-installed so the resolved set never depends on the measuring venv.
